summary: Digital wardrobe and social styling app for cataloging clothes, planning outfits, and tracking wear.
editor_note: The interesting move is turning a closet into a personal data set before asking the user to shop again. Whering removes photo backgrounds, searches a 100M-item catalog, suggests daily outfits, plans packing, and tracks cost per wear. Unlike shopping-led fashion apps, its core loop begins with what someone already owns and adds a social wardrobe graph. The risk is whether cataloging friction and recommendation quality can sustain repeat use beyond novelty.
tags: digital wardrobe,consumer app,personal styling,circular fashion,social commerce
investors: eBay Ventures, Google AI Futures Fund

funding.lead_investor: eBay Ventures and Google AI Futures Fund

product_evidence.claim: The official site lets users add garments from photos, retailer pages, or a database of more than 100 million items, then search and filter the resulting digital wardrobe.
Whering provides daily outfit suggestions, friend wardrobe styling, event and packing planning, plus wear-rate, closet-longevity, and cost-per-wear analytics.

market_context.primary_user: Consumers who want to organize clothes, plan outfits, and reduce unnecessary fashion purchases.
market_context.differentiation: Whering starts with a structured graph of what users already own, then layers styling, planning, analytics, and friend wardrobes on top of it.
market_context.why_now: Better image processing and consumer interest in resale and circular fashion make a persistent digital wardrobe more useful than a static closet inventory.

risks.claim: The falsifiable risk is whether outfit value and social discovery remain high enough to offset the initial work of cataloging a real wardrobe.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment from the official upload, organization, styling, and social workflow.
